newsitem.title: USA: SEC alleges insider trades in Independence Bancorp.
newsitem.headline: SEC alleges insider trades in Independence Bancorp.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday it has charged a former Independence Bancorp Inc director and 11 other individuals from the Philadelphia area with insider trading resulting in illegal trading profits of more than $600,000.

In its complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Philadelphia, the agency alleged Robert Hunter, 66, in prison for unrelated criminal charges, made illegal trades and tipped off a group of friends and relatives about the bank holding company's pending merger with CoreStates Financial Corp.

Also named in the suit were Thomas Pileggi, 52, who resides in Dresher, Pa, and W. Kenneth Greenwood, 65, of Medowbrook, Pa. They were both directors on the board of Cheltenham Bank, a subsidiary of Independence, the SEC said.
In its complaint, the SEC said Hunter not only tipped off other individuals but traded in 40,000 Independence shares himself, profiting illegally by $248,250.

Pileggi, a Philadelphia real estate developer, was accused by the SEC of making an illegal profit of $228,000. Greenwood, who owns a Philadelphia furniture store, was accused of making a profit of $150,412 from illegal trades.
"Mr. Greenwood is reviewing the charges and preserving all of his options," said J. Shane Creamer, Greenwood's attorney. Pileggi and Hunter's attorneys could not be reached for comment.

The nine other defendents in the case were accused by the SEC of buying shares after being tipped off by Hunter. According to the SEC, five have settled the charges without admitting or denying any wrongdoing and have agreed to pay a total of about $80,000 in illegal profits, interest and civil penalties. In June 1994, CoreStates completed its acquisition of Independence.
